title: World Trigger
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Monsters called Neighbors pour through gates into Mikado City, and only the defense agency Border can fight them, using 'Triggers' that swap users' bodies for battle bodies made of trion energy. Low-ranked trainee Osamu Mikumo befriends Yuma Kuga, a powerful Neighbor in disguise, and the two form a squad with Chika, a girl with huge trion reserves. Much of the series follows tactical team ranking battles and the politics of an invasion war.
life_message: It holds up careful planning, teamwork and doing what you believe you should, even when you are the weakest one there.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Disputes go through Border's rules and official rank wars, not personal vendettas.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Border's regulations matter, though Osamu sometimes bends them for conscience.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Defending the whole city comes first; personal searches for family drive some.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: A ranked agency with A, B and C classes; merit decides placement.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Tactics, data and technology drive decisions.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Security of the city outweighs personal expression.

folkways.japan: Rank structures, team harmony, senpai mentorship and an earnest underdog reflect Japanese organizational and shonen norms.

delivery.evidence: Tactics and squad battles carry teamwork themes (AniList Ensemble Cast, Politics); no source comments on delivery (to verify)
delivery.note: Conscience and teamwork come through battle planning rather than stated lessons.

winners_losers: Thoughtful, cooperative squads win; reckless or purely power-driven fighters lose. Sympathy goes to Osamu's conscience and Yuma's openness between worlds.
to_verify: How much real injury happens outside battle bodies
